paras: The warning notice to Black residents of Waxahachie, Texas, was an anonymous hand-lettered notice, found posted near the Central passenger station on the morning of 27 June 1903, that ordered all Black residents to leave the town within four days. The local daily that reported it supposed the notice to be a boy's prank, and no departures, violence or follow-up were reported.

The notice was found on a telephone pole near the Central passenger station and was lettered in pen and ink on a white piece of paper. It read, with its spelling as printed, "LOOK! NEGROS! LOOK! ALL NEGROS ARE WORNED TO LEAVE THIS TOWN IN 4 DAYS IF THEY WANT TO AVOID TRUBEL," and was signed "COMMETY" [committee]. Before it was taken down and handed to a reporter, "a great many negroes" read it, but according to the paper they did not appear to regard it with any seriousness.
The author was not identified, and no report of an investigation, an arrest or anyone leaving the town was found.

The Waxahachie Daily Light ran the story the same day as a brief page-one item headed "A Warning to Negroes," reproducing the notice in full. The paper played the threat down, calling it the supposed "work of some mischievous boy" while suggesting that the misspellings had been made on purpose to conceal the writer's identity. No other white paper and no Black paper is known to have carried the story.
